title: ops pulse handshake handoff notes - week of 2026-10-20
content:
Quick summary:
- Week felt noisy but manageable; three medium incidents, two blips that resolved autoscaling pressure, one deeper outage tied to a recent kernel/driver combo on a subset of Dedicated nodes.
- SLOs mostly green but tail latency for short-chat routes degraded after the driver change. Working hypothesis: kernel/driver + quantized kernel edge case.

Incidents (concise timelines + notes):
1) Incident: Dedicated GPU draining loop (MED) — 2026-10-18 03:10–06:45 UTC
   - Impact: ~3% request latency spikes and ~5% increased error rate for dedicated pools in us-west-2 for ~2.5 hours, followed by rolling restarts.
   - Root cause (current): intermittent GPU driver OOM propagation triggered by our async prefetch path in the runtime. Repro rate ~1/200 requests under specific batching patterns.
   - Mitigation this week: temporary semaphore guard added to prefetch code (hotfix PR merged), rolling restart, node cordon for suspect instance family.
   - Follow-ups: SRE-1452 (driver regression post-rollout) — assigned to Marcus Li. Long-term: driver compatibility test harness for dedicated images.

2) Incident: API gateway 502 cascade (LOW→MED) — 2026-10-19 11:50–12:30 UTC
   - Impact: short spike of 502s served by hosted-api edge for requests with large prompt headers (novel client header pattern).
   - Notes: found malformed keepalive from an edge router config push; reverted config.
   - Action: add header size guard in gateway and new synthetic that exercises large header patterns (owner: Eleanor Chen).

3) Incident: Embeddings rerank job timeouts (LOW) — 2026-10-17 08:00–09:05 UTC
   - Impact: several customer batched embed requests retried by SDK, creating duplicate billing noise.
   - Partial fix: increase client idempotency window and add server-side idempotency keys for long-running embed jobs (PR link in linked_artifacts). Owner: Tomás Rivera.

SLO health snapshot (approximate, last 7d):
- hosted-api request success (p99 latency < 500ms): 99.4% (SLO 99.9%) — degradation window aligns with driver incident
- dedicated-pool throughput SLO (avg tokens/sec): 100% met
- embeddings throughput SLO: 98.6% (SLO 99.5%)
- overall availability (control plane): 99.95%
Notes: need to prioritize p99 latency regression story — low-risk rollback vs. kernel workaround evaluation.

Observability & runbook gaps discovered:
- Missing signal: we lacked a clear metric correlating driver OOMs to per-request KV-cache invalidations. Instrumentation ticket created (SRE-1499).
- Runbook fuzz: the dedicated-node cordon/runbook step assumed automated drain would finish under 15m; observed drains taking up to 40m for large KV caches. Update runbook to include forced-cache-evict step.

Handoff (what next on-call should know):
- Current state: hotfix in prod that gates prefetch path; it's a stopgap and increases tail latency by ~5ms but prevents OOM cascade.
- Do not escalate to infra immediately for reboots; coordinate with Marcus if the semaphore guard trips >3x per hour.
- Watch p99 latency for short-chat route in us-west-2 (dash: /dash/short-chat-p99) and track driver OOM counter (metric name: runtime.gpu.driver_oom).
- If driver_oom > 10 in a rolling 1h window OR p99 degrades >20% vs baseline, trigger bridge and tag: incident-type:driver-oom.

Action items and owners (short):
- Marcus Li: complete driver-compat-test harness spec and start prototyping (due 2026-11-05).
- Eleanor Chen: add large-header synthetic and gateway header-size guard (PR by 2026-10-27).
- Tomás Rivera: finalize server-side idempotency for batch embeddings + SDK patch (release window 2026-10-28).
- Aisha Malik: add p99 alert refinement that suppresses noisy transients from ongoing hotfix; coordinate with Observability (ticket OBS-774).
- Priya Anand: runbook update — forced-cache-evict instructions and estimated drain times (draft by 2026-10-22).

Notes from weekly standup / meeting snippets (informal):
- "We got lucky the initial rollouts were low traffic — could have been worse." — Rana from Deploy
- Observability asked for an example payload that triggers the driver OOM; Devs to produce reproducible minimal repro.
- Cost note: increased retries on embed jobs created ~0.8% incremental spend this week — need tighter client retry policy and server idempotency.

Triage matrix (quick):
- Severity/Impact vs Frequency: driver-oom (MED/LOW-FREQ) -> high chase priority due to blast radius on p99s; gateway-502 (LOW/HIGH-FREQ) -> medium priority with easy rollback; embed-timeouts (LOW/MED-FREQ) -> low priority but billing annoyance.

Planned maintenance & experiments next week:
- Controlled kernel/driver canary in a single dedicated pool with heavy synthetic load (owner: Marcus). Start: 2026-10-26 01:00 UTC.
- Runbook tabletop exercise Thursday to rehearse forced-evict and cordon flows (lead: Priya).

Misc/Notes to self (brain dump):
- Consider adding a per-model KV-cache size metric exposed on /metrics — would help triage large-drain times.
- Revisit autoscaler grace window for dedicated pools; current window accidentally interacts poorly with prefetch semaphore.

Attachment links / refs: see linked_artifacts above. For more context check the deploy slack thread: https://slack-redwood/sre-ops/p-driver-rollout-discussion (internal).

Closing: overall steady but important regression hidden under a driver combo. Priorities: prototype compatibility harness, observability instrumentation, and safer gateway guards. Handoff to next on-call: Eleanor for this weekend (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-25).

Action-item status quick-check (end of doc):
- Marcus Li — driver harness spec: in_progress
- Eleanor Chen — gateway synthetic: open
- Tomás Rivera — idempotency PR: in_review
- Priya Anand — runbook update: draft
- Aisha Malik — p99 alert refinement: in_progress
summary: Weekly SRE update: three incidents (driver OOM on dedicated nodes, gateway 502s, embedding timeouts). Hotfix applied; follow-ups include driver compatibility testing, runbook updates for forced cache eviction, gateway header guards, and idempotency for embeddings. On-call handoff to Eleanor 2026-10-22.
